text:
Andrew Copp is on the trade board. Yahoo Sports listed him there on Nov. 13, and Detroit Sports Nation weighed what he'd be worth to a contender, which is what happens to a 32-year-old veteran on a Red Wings team that has lost seven of its last ten.

He's been producing anyway, with a four-game point streak (one goal, four assists) and 11 points in 22 games, four of them on the power play. His ice time is up to more than 19 minutes a night.

The five-on-five numbers are less kind. Detroit gets about 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, more than three and a half points worse than without him. Last season, Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.3 wins but noted those results ran well ahead of his chances.

What a contender would be buying shows up in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking: 62% of his exits leave the zone with possession, and he's a setup man at 8.5 primary shot assists per 60, 85th percentile among forwards. Watch his minutes. If Detroit starts managing them, that's often the first sign of a move.
